title: DA3408 A4 · AI Image Captioner Observability (vrishab)
description: CPU-only BLIP image captioner: health → application (RED) → clients → system (USE) → correlation. PromQL drafted with AI assistance; prompts logged in build_dashboard.py.

options.content:
**DA3408 A4 · AI image captioner (BLIP, CPU-only).** Read top to bottom: **1 Health** (is it up?) → **2 Application** (throughput · latency · errors) → **3 Clients** (who is calling) → **4 System** (node_exporter: CPU / RAM / disk) → **5 Correlation** (does a bulk upload move the hardware?).  
Colours are the colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette; series also differ by **line style** (solid / dashed / dotted / dash-dot) so they survive greyscale print. Every panel has a title, subtitle, axis label with unit + scale (linear/log) and a story in its ⓘ description. Refresh: 5 s.

panels.title: App · UP / DOWN
panels.description:
UP / DOWN

STORY: Is Prometheus able to scrape the Streamlit app's /metrics? DOWN = app crashed or stopped.

SCALE/UNITS: n/a (single value)

panels.title: node_exporter · UP / DOWN
panels.description:
UP / DOWN

STORY: System metrics source. DOWN = CPU/RAM/disk panels below go blank.

SCALE/UNITS: n/a (single value)

panels.title: Alerts · firing now
panels.description:
firing now

STORY: Count of alert rules currently firing (see rules.yml). 0 = healthy.

SCALE/UNITS: n/a (single value)

panels.title: Model · LOADED / NOT
panels.description:
LOADED / NOT

STORY: BLIP weights resident in RAM. NOT LOADED = first request will be slow.

SCALE/UNITS: n/a (single value)

panels.title: Active requests · in progress now
panels.description:
in progress now

STORY: Uploads currently being processed (single + bulk).

SCALE/UNITS: n/a (single value)

panels.title: Sessions · browser tabs, last 5 min
panels.description:
browser tabs, last 5 min

STORY: Distinct Streamlit sessions seen in the last 5 minutes.

SCALE/UNITS: n/a (single value)

panels.title: Image error ratio · last 1 min
panels.description:
last 1 min

STORY: Failed images / all images over 1 min. Orange > 5 %, vermilion > 20 % (alert threshold).

SCALE/UNITS: percent, 0-100 % (linear)

panels.title: Model memory · RAM used by weights
panels.description:
RAM used by weights

STORY: RSS growth when the model was loaded - the model's own footprint.

SCALE/UNITS: bytes (IEC), single value

options.content: Each image is one unit of work. **Throughput** shows how many are finished per second, **latency** how long each takes (log scale because bulk bursts spread values over decades), **errors** what is failing and **queue** how many images wait for the single model.

panels.title: Throughput · images per second by mode
panels.description:
images per second by mode

STORY: Bulk uploads show as a plateau (steady CPU-bound rate); single uploads as short spikes.

SCALE/UNITS: Images/s; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: Inference latency · p50/p95/p99, log scale
panels.description:
p50/p95/p99, log scale

STORY: p50 is the typical image; a p95/p99 that pulls away from p50 means queueing or oversized images.

SCALE/UNITS: seconds; LOG10 Y axis (bucket-interpolated estimate, accurate to bucket width).

panels.title: Mean latency · s per image (Summary)
panels.description:
s per image (Summary)

STORY: Mean = total inference seconds / images, per mode. Compare with the percentiles: mean >> p50 means a long tail.

SCALE/UNITS: Mean s/image; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: Errors · failures per second by cause
panels.description:
failures per second by cause

STORY: Flat at zero is healthy. Spikes name the cause: corrupt image, bad/empty ZIP, or a model failure.

SCALE/UNITS: Errors/s; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: Queue · active vs waiting for model
panels.description:
active vs waiting for model

STORY: Waiting > 0 means the one-at-a-time CPU model is saturated: users queue and latency rises.

SCALE/UNITS: Count; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: 3 · Clients — who is using the app (custom labels)

options.content: Metrics carry **client_ip**, **session_id** and **browser** labels. The table joins volume and mean latency per client; the bar chart ranks IPs; the time-series splits request rate by browser family (a bounded label, so cardinality stays low). Open the app from a phone/second browser to add clients.

panels.title: Clients · per-IP volume and latency
panels.description:
Per-client usage table

STORY: Who sent how many images and how fast they were served. Built from the labelled Counter and Summary (_sum/_count).

SCALE/UNITS: images = count (linear); latency = seconds (linear).

targets.expr: sum by (client_ip, mode) (captioner_client_inference_seconds_sum) / sum by (client_ip, mode) (captioner_client_inference_seconds_count)

panels.title: By IP · total images
panels.description:
total images

STORY: Longer bar = heavier user. Different IPs appear when the app is opened from another device.

SCALE/UNITS: linear bar length

panels.title: By browser · requests per second
panels.description:
requests per second

STORY: Splits traffic by User-Agent family: useful to spot a single scripted client (curl/python) generating load.

SCALE/UNITS: Requests/s; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

options.content: Hardware view from **node_exporter**. CPU is split into user/system/iowait; RAM and disk are shown with the app's own memory on a second axis; load per core above 1 means runnable work is queueing for a core.

panels.title: CPU · % busy, split by mode
panels.description:
% busy, split by mode

STORY: A bulk ZIP drives user-mode CPU up for the whole batch; iowait stays low because the job is compute-bound.

SCALE/UNITS: CPU %; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: Memory · RAM % (L), app bytes (R)
panels.description:
RAM % (L), app bytes (R)

STORY: RAM used % = 1 - available/total. App RSS (right axis) steps up when the model loads and on large ZIPs.

SCALE/UNITS: RAM used %; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: Disk · used % (L), I/O bytes/s (R)
panels.description:
used % (L), I/O bytes/s (R)

STORY: Used % is capacity pressure; read/write bytes/s show model-cache reads at startup and any swap or log writes.

SCALE/UNITS: Disk used %; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: Saturation · 1-min load per core
panels.description:
1-min load per core

STORY: Above 1.0 means more runnable threads than cores: work is waiting. Normalised by core count so it is comparable across machines.

SCALE/UNITS: Load/core; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: Network · bytes/s in and out
panels.description:
bytes/s in and out

STORY: Shows uploads from other devices (LAN). Uploads from this same machine use loopback and are not counted here.

SCALE/UNITS: Network, B/s; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

options.content: **The point of the assignment:** each panel overlays an application metric (left axis) on a hardware metric (right axis) with a shared crosshair. Start a bulk ZIP and watch throughput/active requests rise **together with** CPU; when the batch ends both fall back.

panels.title: Throughput vs CPU · img/s (L), CPU % (R)
panels.description:
img/s (L), CPU % (R)

STORY: Throughput rising and CPU rising together proves the workload is CPU-bound.

SCALE/UNITS: Images/s; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: Active requests vs app CPU · count (L), % of one core (R)
panels.description:
count (L), % of one core (R)

STORY: App CPU (100 % = one core fully used) tracks active requests; values over 100 % mean multi-threaded inference.

SCALE/UNITS: Active requests; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: p95 latency vs CPU · seconds (L), CPU % (R)
panels.description:
seconds (L), CPU % (R)

STORY: When CPU saturates, p95 latency climbs: the dashboard's saturation-to-user-impact link.

SCALE/UNITS: p95 latency, s; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).

panels.title: Bulk progress vs memory · % done (L), app bytes (R)
panels.description:
% done (L), app bytes (R)

STORY: Progress climbs 0 → 100 % per ZIP; memory should plateau (no leak). A steady upward drift across batches would signal a leak.

SCALE/UNITS: Batch %; linear Y axis; X axis = time (local).
